sources.excerpt: The official homepage identifies three distinct locations: Columbia Heights Restaurant & Bar, Shaw Restaurant & Mart, and Bethesda Cuisine.
The official Shaw page identifies Chercher Ethiopian Restaurant & Mart at 1334 9th St NW, Washington, DC 20001.
The Owner-powered ordering surface is explicitly titled Chercher Restaurant Shaw - Restaurant & Mart, shows 1334 9th St NW, and lists the current Mart menu including Groceries.

The generic menu resolves to the Columbia Heights Restaurant & Bar catalog, confirmed by its Columbia Heights footer and the location-specific /menu/chercherethiopian-bar route; it is out of scope for the Shaw Mart record.

The current official sitemap lists the three location pages, menu, catering, tags, story, events, careers, gift cards, locations, contact, and private events; it exposes no allergen, nutrition, ingredient, FAQ, PDF, or download page.
A search-indexed legacy DC menu PDF path was inspected but now returns 404 after redirecting to the current domain; it is not a current allergen source.
The official site links this OrderSave application download surface; inspection found no allergen, nutrition, ingredient, or cross-contact disclosure.

Targeted searches combining the restaurant name and domain with allergen, allergy, nutrition, ingredients, PDF, and menu returned current menu/location pages and obsolete menu PDFs, but no current official allergen matrix or cross-contact statement.

proposedChanges: Replace the mixed generic-menu projection with the location-specific Shaw Restaurant & Mart product boundary from /menu/chercherethiopian-mart; exclude three Columbia Heights-only frozen products and two non-product artifacts.
Add the 21 current Mart products absent from the frozen catalog, including the Groceries section and Mart-only sides, drinks, and combo products; consolidate repeated Most ordered presentations.
Normalize the Mart-specific names and categories while preserving explicit linked-menu fish positives and the Egg side positive.

Remove unsupported direct wheat/gluten and milk/egg claims derived only from generic food names such as pasta or cheesecake; no current official matrix or cross-contact disclosure was found after all four required searches, so all other products remain unavailable for direct allergen evidence.
